title: The launcher window shows the install and the server it found, and its Play starts the client at the window size the run asks for
notes: The launcher is started with --window-ui rather than --wait, so the run opens the window a player meets and
starts no client of its own: the scenario reads the window through UI Automation and presses its Play the same
way, by the button's accessible name, with no cursor, no foreground and no global input.
The ready screen's bar shows the server as host:port, the client's revision and the window size as WxH, each a value
of its own, beside the login server's status, which reads Online once the launcher's own first run has reached the
scratch login server; the one primary button is named for the launcher's state, so it is called Play only once that
first run is done, and pressing it by name waits for that. The settings screen, opened with its Settings button and
left with Back, the one in the header, shows the installation as
a value under the label Installation, which must be exactly the install the driver found itself through
launcher --dry-run, {install}, taken literally in the pattern.
Play must start the client as a child of the launcher with a client area of the size the references were measured at.
The run's install check still holds: the window writes its place and its web view profile in the Ambrose data
No game server runs here, so the login server's two warnings about empty creation and realm tables are expected.
server_log_allowed: character_create_school holds no school, so no wizard can be created until it does
realmlist holds no realm, so no player can be sent to a gameserver until one is added

steps.name: the ready screen shows the server, the client, the window size and the server online
the settings screen shows the install it found
go back to the ready screen
press Play in the launcher window
the client brings its renderer up
the login window is on the screen
